title: She has no priest to flirt with, he thought with conscious bitterness, remembering how he had seen her last.
html_source:
Stephen has issues seeing women as only two things: virgins and whores. This stems from his obsession with the Virgin Mary in earlier parts of the book and his frequent escapades with prostitutes.

Emma is his muse, his pure and virginal muse, who, like Mary is his obsession. Seeing her ‘flirt’ with the priest suggests that she is not as pure and virginal as he would like and he struggles to allow these different labels to exist in her.
